name: FL-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: Republican candidate has massive fundraising edge
Open seat with no incumbent on ballot
model.rationale: This southwest Florida seat sits about fourteen points to the right of the nation, and the Republican nominee has outraised the Democrat roughly forty-five to one. Markets price the Republican at about 94 percent, consistent with a comfortable double-digit margin.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending or an unusually strong Democratic fundraising quarter could narrow the gap, but the structural lean is hard to overcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Byron Donalds (R) is not on the ballot.

overview: Byron Donalds is leaving the seat to run for governor, but the district's fundamentals remain firmly Republican. The seat leans about fourteen points to the right, and the 2024 environment favored the GOP here by an even wider margin. The Republican nominee, Jim Schwartzel, has raised over two million dollars and holds a large cash advantage, while Democrat Victor Arias has raised under fifty thousand. Prediction markets give the Republican roughly a 94 percent chance of holding the seat. No public polls or expert ratings are available, so the forecast leans on the district's partisan lean and the money gap. The open-seat dynamic removes the incumbent's personal vote but does little to change the underlying partisanship. A Republican hold by a double-digit margin is the clear expectation.
